_readme: One provider cell for every feature ID in features.json.

sharedNotes.text:
Pi extensions provide these features:
   - Plan mode and plan approval: [pi-plan-mode](https://pi.dev/packages/@narumitw/pi-plan-mode)
   - Session goal: [pi-goal-x](https://pi.dev/packages/pi-goal-x)
   - To-do list: [rpiv-todo](https://pi.dev/packages/@juicesharp/rpiv-todo)
   - Agent questions: [rpiv-ask-user-question](https://pi.dev/packages/@juicesharp/rpiv-ask-user-question)
   - MCP prompts: [pi-mcp-adapter](https://pi.dev/packages/pi-mcp-adapter)
   - Subagent tabs: [pi-subagents](https://pi.dev/packages/@tintinweb/pi-subagents)

   Pi's plan mode is a setting of the extension, not a setting of the provider, so **Shift+Tab** does not toggle it. Type the extension's `/plan` command to start planning.

ZCode takes an image attachment only on a model that declares image input (see [Attachments](#attachments)). A tool result arrives as text, and LeapMux restores the picture from ZCode's stored attachment records.
Codewhale and Cline build tool results as text only, so no tool result can carry a picture.

Amp has no plan mode, to-do tool, session goal or MCP input request. Its question tool (`ask_user_choice`) cannot be answered in stream-JSON mode: the session ends, so LeapMux keeps the tool off. The stream also carries no child messages and no workflow activity. An Amp MCP result is text only; a `Read` of an image file does render.
On these LeapMux paths, native compaction produces no completed event that the chat renders as a notice. A running status or a smaller next context alone does not count.
Kiro shows a rate-limit notice row ("The model service is busy"), not rate-limit state.

Oh My Pi has plan mode and a session goal, but LeapMux cannot reach them. The `rpc-ui` mode that LeapMux drives has no mode command, and `/plan` and `/goal` are TUI-only. Tracked upstream: [oh-my-pi#8171](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/8171) and [oh-my-pi#9230](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/9230).

For Kilo, OpenCode, Reasonix and Codewhale, the plan arrives with no approval request. Switch the mode back to start the work. Kiro switches back to Default mode and starts the work itself. Codewhale's plan mode refuses edits and commands. Cline discusses the plan in the chat first: say it is good and the banner appears. Dirac's plan card resolves at the next prompt instead of raising an approval banner, so there is no **Approve** to press.
GitHub Copilot and Cline carry one question per request.
Goose and Reasonix raise no native agent question request. Dirac's ACP path exposes no agent question to LeapMux.

Kimi Code's MCP clients negotiate no elicitation, so an MCP server cannot ask for input. Cursor's ACP bridge supplies no MCP elicitation handler, so its client declines a form request. OpenCode and Kilo declare no elicitation capability (tracked upstream: [opencode#23066](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/23066)). Qwen Code does not implement it (upstream work on the `feat/mcp-elicitation-support` branch). Codewhale, ZCode, Oh My Pi and Cline carry no MCP input request that LeapMux renders.
Cursor offers Agent, Plan, and Ask modes only. OpenCode and Kilo have no permission-mode axis. Pi has no permission controls.

Amp's Mode picks the model and the effort, so Amp offers no Model or Reasoning effort. A thread keeps Amp's mode of its first message; start a new session to use another mode. Cursor's effort rides its model ids, so Cursor offers no Reasoning effort. ZCode's own `auto` mode is not offered: the shipped build denies every tool call under it.
Claude Code (Haiku), GitHub Copilot, ZCode, Kiro and Cline offer Reasoning effort only when the chosen model offers levels.

Claude Code, Goose, Kilo, Qwen Code and Grok Build take a goal only when their CLI advertises its `goal` command. Kimi Code takes one only while the engine's goal feature runs. Reasonix sets a goal only in Goal mode; otherwise it can only clear one. Kiro needs a live goal run before it can clear, pause, or resume the goal. It works for at most five rounds, then pauses the goal. Resume it to continue. Qwen Code's `/loop` command and its scheduled prompts are off in LeapMux.

The Interrupt control of a subagent tab is what `SupportsChildInterrupt` reports. Claude Code stops a child through its `stop_task` control request, on the CLI's own task id. A provider that reports no interrupt leaves the child tab without that control.

Cursor's protocol exposes no steer method. The installed Goose ACP handshake advertises no steer method, so LeapMux offers Preempt. Reasonix steers only when its CLI advertises a steer method. Qwen Code takes a steer at its next tool gap.

A prompt's buttons, scopes and timeouts come from the provider. Codex's **Allow as** offers **Once**, **Session**, **Command rule**, or **Host rule**. ZCode's "always" option writes a permission rule for the project. Codewhale denies an approval that nobody answers within 300 seconds. Text that you type before Amp's **Deny** reaches the agent as the reason. When a Copilot CLI refuses LeapMux's safe default, LeapMux reopens the session in Manual.

Kiro's prompts follow its own rules. Its scope applies to **Deny** as well: **Always** with **Deny** refuses the same call in every workspace until you remove the rule in Kiro's settings. Kiro runs the working directory's hooks (`.kiro/hooks/`) without asking. In Supervised Autopilot, a turn ends with a review of its file changes: **Allow** keeps them, **Deny** restores each file. Its **Content Collection** setting decides whether Kiro may use your session content to improve its service.
Cline uses your own Cline settings, credentials, and stored sessions. Do not continue one session in your own Cline and in LeapMux at the same time: each one rewrites the stored conversation.

A Cline agent can run scheduled Cline automations. Its subagents run tools without a prompt. Approve a spawn only for a task you trust. Cline hooks and plugins run only in **Auto-approve**. Cline runs them without asking.

Cursor, Kilo, OpenCode, Pi and Reasonix deliver the subagent's transcript when it completes: the prompt at spawn and the report at the end. A background spawn of Kilo, OpenCode or Reasonix keeps the prompt only.
Cline streams one subagent live. When two run at the same time, their transcripts appear when they finish.

A transcript streams at message boundaries: a long text run appears when its message or turn ends. Goose streams the child's tool rows only, and its text never arrives. ZCode streams the tool cards live and sends the child's text as the final report. Codewhale and Qwen Code tail a transcript file, with about half a second of lag.

Fast Agent receives a composer PDF as an ACP embedded resource. Its `attach_media` tool stages media through a separate path. Fast Agent sends image blocks in ACP tool results, but it does not accept a generic binary composer attachment.
Fast Agent can ask for permission before shell commands, MCP calls, and local filesystem tools.
Junie's plan mode is a `mode` config option. Its review appears as a separate request. After approval, an ACP plan update fills the to-do list.

Factory Droid's plan surface is its Spec mode. `ExitSpecMode` is the approval. Missions (its multi-agent workflows) are a one-shot `exec` surface and are refused on the streaming input LeapMux drives, so no workflow grouping appears.
Junie raises a question as a permission-shaped request with one option per choice: questions and permissions share one channel in 26.9.22.
Fast Agent registers no elicitation callback on the ACP path, so an MCP server cannot ask for input.
Fast Agent's `agent` mode axis selects the agent. The Mode chip shows that choice. Its native policy controls permission prompts.
Dirac sends no standalone to-do update. Its plan entries are the only checklist, and they arrive with no approval request.

Dirac and Fast Agent open a child tab for each subagent. The tab shows its prompt and loads the native message history when the child ends. Neither agent streams its full child transcript while it runs. Fast Agent's [Agent Client Protocol (ACP) tracker](https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/blob/07c460ee395843b91e2bf71a5136f0b6b2886852/src/fast_agent/acp/tool_progress.py#L236-L260) creates a tool ID that differs from the model ID in its [child snapshot](https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/blob/07c460ee395843b91e2bf71a5136f0b6b2886852/src/fast_agent/agents/subagent_tool.py#L829-L833). Its [ACP completion](https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/blob/07c460ee395843b91e2bf71a5136f0b6b2886852/src/fast_agent/acp/tool_progress.py#L873-L900) sends result text without a child ID. When equal results cannot identify one archive, LeapMux closes the ambiguous child with an archive-unavailable report.

Junie advertises steering (`_meta.steering.supported`) but offers no steer method in its ACP catalog. LeapMux steers by queueing a follow-up prompt, which starts the next turn rather than inserting into the running one.
Letta Code's `Workflow` tool exists in the toolset but emits no workflow grouping events on the wire. A background process summary can carry `kind:"workflow"`, and LeapMux draws no group from it.

Claude Code's TUI can send a message to a Task subagent. It queues the message while the child runs or resumes an idle child. LeapMux drives Claude over stream-json stdin. Its user message carries no child or task ID, so typed input reaches the root session. The child tab is read-only. A direct subagent wire path is required to change this.

The Bypass permissions shortcut is the plus-menu / banner control that switches the session to the provider's own bypass mode. A provider whose plugin declares no permission preset renders no shortcut, whatever its CLI can do. Junie, Dirac, Qoder and Fast Agent are in that group today.
Junie, Letta Code, and Qoder CLI state on the wire that a child takes no further input. CodeBuddy Code's stream-JSON path offers no child-directed input route. Their child tabs are read-only.
Junie can clear a session goal from the goal card. It creates a goal through its own elicitation, so the card cannot set one.
OpenCode and Kilo accept an ACP binary resource, but their configured model adapter rejects its `application/octet-stream` file part. LeapMux refuses that attachment before the turn starts.
Qoder's prompt parser ignores inline PDF and binary blocks. Its file-upload path requires a separate file identifier that LeapMux does not create.
Codex keeps its `update_plan` tool off unless its config enables it. When enabled, LeapMux shows its updates in the To-do sidebar.
LeapMux receives no rate-limit state from CodeBuddy Code's stream-JSON integration. A model error can still end a turn, but the Agent info card shows no rate-limit window.
CodeBuddy Code offers a Bypass permissions shortcut. Its LeapMux plugin declares no Smart permissions shortcut.
CodeBuddy Code declines MCP server elicitation in the stream-JSON mode that LeapMux drives. No input form reaches LeapMux on that path.
Goose converts ACP text resources and images. Its ACP bridge drops embedded blob resources, so LeapMux refuses PDF and other binary attachments before the turn starts.
Codex offers its `request_user_input` question tool in Plan mode. Its default mode does not offer that tool.
Pi's MCP adapter presents each form field as a separate question and asks for a final review. LeapMux relays those questions instead of drawing one form card.
CodeBuddy Code runs `/compact` in stream-JSON mode, but that stream reports no compaction notice. LeapMux cannot show a notice for it.
Junie's ACP bridge sends no thought update for a Responses reasoning item. The model answer still reaches LeapMux.
The installed Cursor CLI's ACP bridge sends no usage update after a model turn. LeapMux cannot show the context count on this path.
On LeapMux's current GitHub Copilot model path, a generic binary blob reaches the CLI but only its filename reaches the model. LeapMux refuses the blob before the turn.

Dirac's ACP `session/load` reuses the session ID and settings. A completed task starts a new task on the next prompt. [Dirac's ACP handler](https://github.com/dirac-run/dirac/blob/46d33ad610ef5135ff2339611eac21a3aeadcd47/cli/src/agent/DiracAgent.ts#L1775-L1789) specifies this behavior. An unfinished task has no history row until it ends. A reattached prompt then starts fresh. The next model request carries neither task's earlier messages. LeapMux restores chat rows saved by a prior tab on this Worker, but Dirac does not send those rows to the model.
The installed Cursor CLI's ACP bridge replaces embedded PDF and binary resources with a filename and a notice that it omitted the bytes. LeapMux refuses these attachments before the turn.

The installed Copilot CLI sends a PDF as filename text on LeapMux's configured model path, even with Sonnet selected. PDF document blocks require an Anthropic provider that LeapMux does not configure. LeapMux refuses PDFs before the turn.
The installed MiMo Code 0.1.15 CLI declines MCP elicitation without sending LeapMux a form request. LeapMux cannot show an input form on this path.
CodeBuddy Code sends Read image bytes to its model through a separate input. Its stream gives LeapMux only a text placeholder for that tool result, so the tool row cannot show the image.
Qwen Code converts a Read image for its model, but its ACP tool update carries text without image bytes. LeapMux cannot show the image in that tool row.
Reasonix sends a `view_image` picture to its model, but its ACP tool update contains text only. LeapMux cannot show the image in that tool row.

CodeBuddy Code's stream-JSON tool set does not offer `AskUserQuestion` in Default or Bypass mode. Its ToolSearch cannot add that tool. A native attempt returns a tool-not-found result, so LeapMux receives no question banner.

CodeBuddy Code accepts text while it works. Its stream-JSON steering path converts `control_request/steer.content_blocks` to text. A queued PNG filename reaches the model as text, but the image bytes do not.
Claude Code emits rate-limit state for Claude subscriber OAuth sessions. API-key sessions ignore the subscriber rate-limit headers, so their Agent info card shows no subscriber window.

Junie's ACP child-session updates support subagent rows and tabs. Its Bash tool reports a terminal call but no stable background-process status route, so LeapMux shows a tool card without a background shell row.
Qoder reports context occupancy as a ratio. LeapMux shows its percentage in Agent info without inventing token totals when Qoder omits them.
The installed ZCode app server has no `session/steer` method. Its `session/send` returns a busy error while a prompt runs, so LeapMux queues the message for the next turn instead of offering Steer.

Qoder emits a `compact_boundary` after successful native compaction. It refuses `/compact` when its token count says the summary would not reduce context. A short session or a model that reports too few input tokens can cause this refusal. A refusal shows no completed notice.

Qoder exposes account Credits through a [separate usage control](https://docs.qoder.com/cli/sdk/cost-usage). Its stream-JSON integration does not forward model response rate-limit headers to LeapMux, which does not show Credits quota as a rate-limit window.

Qoder sends workflow child task starts but no child message frames on stream JSON. LeapMux shows each child prompt while it runs. When the workflow finishes, LeapMux loads each saved child transcript from Qoder's journal.
Factory Droid emits an `llm_retry` event after a model HTTP 429. Its stream reports no quota window, remaining amount, utilization or reset time. LeapMux shows no rate-limit window for that retry.

Factory Droid's MCP tool can ask its server for `elicitation/create`, but the installed CLI answers `-32601 Method not found`. It sends no form request through stream JSON-RPC, so LeapMux cannot show an MCP input form.
Fast Agent accepts `--model` when LeapMux starts its ACP process. Its `session/new` reports modes but no model catalog or model option. The session offers no Model chip or [+] menu group.
Fast Agent's coding agent offers no to-do tool and sends no ACP `plan` update. Its separate IterativePlanner sends plan updates, but LeapMux starts the coding agent.
Junie loads MCP tools, but its client answers `elicitation/create` with `-32601 Server does not support elicitation/create`. It sends no form request to LeapMux.
Letta Code sends a `ViewImage` picture to its model. The installed App Server removes image blocks from live and stored tool results before LeapMux receives them.
Junie sends an MCP tool's PNG bytes to its model, but its ACP tool call and update carry `content:[]`. LeapMux receives no image bytes to show in the tool row.

Claude Code runs a Workflow child but sends LeapMux only the top-level workflow task row. ZCode sends a workflow task without group metadata. Codewhale and Qwen send one self-grouped workflow row but no separate child or stage row. One row does not group work.

qwen-code.notes: Qwen replaces unsupported binary media with a document placeholder in its model request. The model does not receive the file bytes.

codex.notes: Codex keeps the original user prompts in the next model request after native compaction. It replaces the earlier assistant turns with a handoff summary.

cursor.notes: Cursor sends `/compact` to the model as ordinary text on LeapMux's ACP path. It emits no native compaction result.

github-copilot.notes: Copilot removes the old standalone turns. Its native summary can quote the original user prompt, so the prompt text can remain inside the summary.

reasonix.notes: Reasonix sends `/compact` to the model as ordinary text on LeapMux's ACP path. Its desktop command is unavailable on that path.

amp.notes: Amp sends `/compact` to the model as ordinary text in stream mode. It emits no native compaction result.

cline.notes: Cline's hub treats `/compact` as a model prompt. The CLI's local command is unavailable through the hub connection that LeapMux drives.

junie.notes: Junie acknowledges `/compress`, but the next two native model requests still contain the older issue and its solution. This ACP path makes no summary request.

letta-code.notes: The installed Letta App Server sends `/compact` to the model as ordinary text and emits no native compaction result.

dirac.notes: Dirac uses `/smol` for manual compaction. Its native `condense` tool replaces old context before the next model request.

fast-agent.notes: Fast Agent's ACP path returns `Unknown command: /compact` for the manual command.

cursor.notes: Cursor keeps prior context on its server. LeapMux resumes the same native conversation ID, so the earlier turns remain available to the model.

qoder-cli.notes: Qoder runs a read-only shell command without a prompt in Default mode. It asks before a write or another call that its policy requires.

letta-code.notes: The installed Letta App Server ignores a project MCP server on LeapMux's path and offers no local MCP tool to the model.

dirac.notes: Dirac's ACP path offers no tool from a configured project MCP server.

factory-droid.notes:
Factory Droid offers these reasoning levels:
- `none`
- `low`
- `medium`
- `high`

codebuddy-code.notes:
CodeBuddy Code offers six modes. Startup advertises these four:
- **Default**
- **Accept Edits**
- **Plan**
- **Bypass Permissions**

letta-code.notes:
Letta Code offers these modes:
- **Standard**
- **Accept Edits**
- **Unrestricted**
- **Strict**

factory-droid.notes:
Factory Droid's Mode axis controls autonomy:
- **Default** asks before changes.
- **Spec** writes a plan.
- **Auto (Low)** allows limited automatic work.
- **Auto (Medium)** allows more automatic work.
- **Auto (High)** allows the most automatic work.

kimi-code.notes: Kimi Code accepts a typed message from its subagent tab while the child runs.

mimo-code.notes: MiMo Code accepts a typed message from its subagent tab while the child runs.

factory-droid.notes: Factory Droid accepts a typed message from its subagent tab while the child runs.

letta-code.notes: LeapMux has no native mid-turn steering route for Letta Code on its App Server path.
